title: Scientists Solved Why Some Frogs Survive a Fungus That's Wiped Out Amphibians Worldwide
hook: A fungus has driven amphibian populations to collapse across the globe — but some frogs bounce back, and researchers just found out how.
key_points: A deadly chytrid fungus has devastated amphibian populations worldwide, yet some populations mysteriously recover.
Surviving frogs develop powerful immune defenses while still tadpoles — before the fungus even gets a chance to attack after metamorphosis.
That head start appears to be the key difference between populations that collapse and populations that rebound.
The study also uncovered a large set of previously unknown antimicrobial peptides in these frogs, which could inspire new infection-fighting drugs.
content_html: A fungal disease has wiped out amphibian populations across the planet, but a puzzling minority of frogs keep bouncing back. Researchers just figured out their secret.
extra_html: Survivor frogs build strong immune defenses while they're still tadpoles, well before the chytrid fungus gets its chance to attack after metamorphosis — a head start that appears to make the difference between a population that collapses and one that recovers. Digging into how those defenses work, the researchers uncovered a large, previously unknown collection of antimicrobial peptides — small proteins with infection-fighting properties — that could someday inspire new drugs against other infections, not just this fungus.

related.title: How Immunity Works
related.hook: Your body fights invaders on two fronts: a fast, general first response that hits anything foreign, and a slower, custom-built defense that learns and remembers each specific enemy.

related.title: Antibodies and Immune Memory
related.hook: The first time a germ infects you, your body fights from scratch. The second time, it remembers — and crushes the invader before you ever feel sick.

flashcards.back_html: Surviving populations develop strong immune defenses while still tadpoles — before the fungus can attack after metamorphosis — giving them a head start.

flashcards.prompt: What else did the study uncover while investigating these frogs' immune defenses?

A vaccine already approved for human use

flashcards.explanation_html: Antimicrobial peptides are small infection-fighting proteins; finding a large, new collection of them opens a path toward new drug leads, not just an explanation for frog survival.

flashcards.prompt: Why could this discovery matter beyond amphibians?
flashcards.back_html: The newly found antimicrobial peptides could someday inspire new drugs to fight other infections, not just the chytrid fungus.
